about: The fight camera of the old build's arena rounds — with stab mode and magic as its campaign fights have them — written by tools/extract_camera.mjs and read by js/view/camera.js. Do not edit by hand.

Space: metres, Y up, the enemy at the origin facing +Z, the hero on the +Z axis facing -Z. Positions of shots are in that frame; `position` of an animation and `location` of a shake are in the camera's own frame (three.js: +X right, +Y up, -Z forward).

Angles: `euler` curves are [roll, pitch, yaw] in rotation units (65536 = one turn; yaw to the right, pitch up) and are cut to whole units when used; shake rotations are radians; fields of view are horizontal degrees of the 3:2 picture.

Cues: `group` sorts them (round, hero, clash, stab, magic, enemy); `when` says when the old fight has the moment, `does` what the camera does; `do` / `variants` (picked by the option named in `option`; a list may differ by size) are the actions camera.js carries out.

Curves: keys { t, v, a, l, m } sorted by t — value, arrive / leave slope per second, and how the stretch to the next key is filled: curve (cubic Hermite), linear or constant (default linear; a missing slope is 0).

units.derivation: the new hero's Head bone is 1.569 m above his feet in rest pose; the old hero's b_MF_Head is 130.01819388367196 old units above his (B_Player.Mesh.Birthright_Player_Mesh)

fightStart.when: The intro is over and the fighting begins. Fire it on the frame after the intro shot has played out — FightCamera.introDone says when.
fightStart.does: Cuts to the fight view over the hero's shoulder. After the delay (game time) the handheld sway starts and loops until roundOver.

roundOver.when: The round has played out: the loser's short death is over and the screen is black (old build: 1.64 x the dying clip's length after the fatal blow).
roundOver.does: The sway fades out. Nothing else is stopped.

pause.when: The pause menu opens (do not call update() while the game is paused).
pause.does: Drops every running shake at once.

heroSlash.when: The hero starts a slash. `from` says where the blade comes from as the hero sees it (a swipe to the right is a slash from the left): leftLow, leftMid, leftHigh, centerLeft, centerMid, centerRight, rightHigh, rightMid, rightLow, downRight, downMid, downLeft; or big for the slash that completes a combo.
heroSlash.does: A short push of the camera along the swing, until heroSlashEnd. A combo-finishing slash has none.

heroSlashEnd.when: The slash is over: its clip has ended and 0.2 s have passed, or something else took its place (the next slash, a block, a dodge, a hit, a clash).
heroSlashEnd.does: Fades the slash's camera push out.

heroSlashHit.when: The hero's blade cuts the enemy — full hits and scratches alike, at the slash's hit moment.

heroSlashBlocked.when: The enemy's guard stops the hero's slash (the hero recoils).

heroSlashMissed.when: The slash reaches its hit moment and cannot hurt the enemy: it is invulnerable in mid-attack, or already falling.

heroParry.when: The hero's slash parries the enemy's attack: the first instant of his parry move. Not when the parry fails, nor when it turns into a sword clash.

heroBlock.when: An enemy attack lands on the hero's raised shield (also when the shield breaks or the attack cannot be blocked).
heroBlock.does: Fades out the recoil of the block before, if it still runs, and starts a new recoil of the camera.

heroBlockEnd.when: The hero's block recoil has finished, or he leaves the block while it still plays. Not when no recoil is playing.

heroDodge.when: The hero starts a dodge; `side` is left or right.
heroDodge.does: The camera leans with him until heroDodgeEnd.

heroDodgeEnd.when: Twice per dodge: when the hero starts to come back (the button is released after 0.2 s, or 0.6 s are up), and again when the dodge is over or cut short by anything.
heroDodgeEnd.does: Fades the lean out; a second call while it still fades starts the fade again from full.

heroHit.when: The hero is hit and starts to flinch. `forced` is true when the flinch is not the ordinary one for the blow: hit while dodging, hit while stabbing out of a dodge, or thrown back after losing a sword clash.
heroHit.does: Recoil of the camera until heroHitEnd. A forced flinch only has it once an ordinary hit has happened earlier in the round.

heroHitEnd.when: The flinch ends (0.2 s before its clip does) or is replaced: by a block, by another hit, by the hero's death.

heroShieldBash.when: The super move's shield bash lands on the enemy (old clip: 0.95 s in).

heroDefeated.when: The hero's health runs out: he starts to fall.
heroDefeated.does: The camera sinks away over the next seconds; it is never stopped.

clashStart.when: A sword clash begins: the enemy answers a parry by locking blades.
clashStart.does: Asks for the clash view: the camera pushes in on the locked blades. Served on the next update.

clashEnd.when: The clash is over, whoever won (also when it ends because the enemy dies).
clashEnd.does: Asks for the fight view again.

stabStart.when: Stab mode opens: the enemy answers a parry by reeling with a weak spot exposed.
stabStart.does: Asks for a stab view. No battle level of the old build has one — for any enemy size, campaign or arena — so the request only stops the fight view: from the second update on the picture stands still (sway and shakes included) until stabEnd.

weakSpotShown.when: A weak spot lights up on the enemy. `quick` false: in stab mode, a moment after stabStart and again for every further stab of a chain. `quick` true: a spot that flashes up in the middle of one of the enemy's special attacks, outside stab mode.

false.note: Just before the spot shows, the reeling enemy slows the game to 0.125; it stays there until the hero stabs (heroStab) or the chance passes (stabTimeout).

true.note: If the game runs at full speed it slows to 0.3 (plus 0.01 per enemy level above 20, at most 1) while the spot shows — half a second of the attack's clip — and returns to full speed when the spot goes or is tapped.

heroStab.when: The hero stabs a weak spot — in stab mode or as a quick stab: 0.12 s into his stab move, an instant before it goes in.

clock.note: From the tap on the weak spot (the start of the stab move) a stab in stab mode runs the game at 0.5 until it lands. A quick stab does not slow the game.

stabHit.when: A stab in stab mode goes in: 0.05 s (game time) after the stab move's hit moment.

clock.note: The game drops to 0.025 and stands still for 0.133 s (hit pause); 0.25 s of real time after the pause it is back at full speed. After the last stab of a chain it goes to full speed at once instead (only the pause stays), and stabEnd follows in the same instant.

quickStabHit.when: A quick stab goes in (the stab at a spot that flashed up during an attack): the stab move's hit moment.

clock.note: 0.115 s later (game time) the game drops to 0.025 for 0.175 s of real time and stands still for 0.083 s — the feedback of a heavy hit.

stabTimeout.when: The chance to stab passes unused: the reeling enemy's slow motion ends and the hero has not started a stab. (A stab cannot fail in any other way in the old build.)
stabTimeout.does: Nothing on the camera; the picture stays still until stabEnd, when the enemy has finished reeling.

stabEnd.when: Stab mode is over: the last stab of a chain has gone in, or the enemy has finished reeling without being stabbed, or something else took it out of its reeling (the super move, its death).
stabEnd.does: Asks for the fight view again: it is back on the next update.

clock.note: Full speed, whatever slow motion was left.

magicStart.when: The hero enters casting: the magic button is used with a full meter and the interface goes to its cast mode.
magicStart.does: Nothing on the camera: no cut, no animation — the fight view simply runs in slow motion. Nothing happens while the gesture is drawn either.

clock.note: The game runs at 0.6 for 0.75 s of real time, then at full speed again; magicCast and magicCancel end it sooner.

magicCast.when: A drawn gesture is recognised: the hero starts the spell's cast move (and the enemy is held in a flinch until the spell is done).

magicRelease.when: The spell goes off: 1.05 s into the cast move of an attack spell (fire, electric, ice, poison, light, dark) — the blast appears on the enemy; 0.95 s into the heal's; 0.96 s into the shield spell's.
magicRelease.does: Small shake, the same for every spell.

magicHit.when: An attack spell's damage lands, 0.8 s (game time) after magicRelease.

magicCancel.when: Casting ends without a spell: no gesture was recognised, the hero was hit while drawing, or the pause menu opened.

enemyAttack.when: The enemy starts an attack: every attack of a set (a special attack counts once, at its first swing) and every parry counter. `move` names the camera move; `usedBy` lists which old attacks used which, per size (in brackets: where the blade comes from as the hero sees it).
enemyAttack.does: Plays the move once; it is not stopped when the attack is cut short.

enemyHit.when: An enemy attack hits the hero (also the blow that follows a lost sword clash).
enemyHit.does: Big shake; long big shake against a large enemy.

enemyBlocked.when: The enemy's blocked swing bounces off the hero's shield, a moment after heroBlock. Not for an attack that cannot be blocked; for the last attack of a set only if the block leaves the enemy open. `broken` is true when the shield had no points left.
enemyBlocked.does: Shield-block shake (big shake for a large enemy's clean block).

enemyMiss.when: An enemy attack reaches its hit moment and does not hit: the hero dodged it, or his parry protects him. (The old clips also play it by themselves: medium: Attack_Special_08 at 2.60 s.)

enemyGroundTap.when: The enemy's weapon knocks on the ground during a move. Old clips — medium: Attack_Special_05 at 3.79 s; Death_Universal at 2.29 s | large: Attack_Big_Center at 0.51 s; Attack_Big_Left at 0.50 s; Attack_Big_Right at 0.54 s; Attack_Special_02 at 0.85 s, 2.65 s | mediumDual: Attack_Special_04 at 2.67 s; Attack_Special_08 at 2.75 s.
enemyGroundTap.does: Small shake for a medium enemy, big shake for a large one, nothing for a small one.

enemyGroundSlam.when: A large enemy's weapon or body slams the ground. Old clips — large: Attack_Big_Center at 1.35 s; Attack_Big_Down at 0.51 s; Attack_Parried_Center at 0.82 s; Attack_Small_Center at 0.82 s; Attack_Special_01 at 5.60 s; Attack_Special_03 at 4.05 s; Attack_Special_04 at 0.83 s, 2.73 s, 4.06 s; Attack_Special_05 at 0.83 s, 2.66 s; Attack_Special_06 at 0.83 s, 2.72 s; Attack_Special_09 at 4.42 s; Death_Universal at 3.37 s; SwordGrind_BossWin at 0.42 s.

enemyBurst.when: The electric burst of one large enemy (the golem) as it collapses. Old clips — large: Death_Universal at 0.34 s.

other.roundIntro: Not a cue: FightCamera.begin(size) starts the round with the enemy's entrance shot (letterboxed, fading in from black).
other.enemyDefeated: Nothing happens to the camera when the enemy falls: the fight view and the sway go on until roundOver.
other.slowMotionAndHitPause: Not cues: pass the game speed to update(dt, gameSpeed) — below 1 in slow motion, 0 during a hit pause. Shots (intro, clash push-in) run on game time; animations and shakes run on real time.
other.early: Any cue takes the option early: true — "this is the player's input taking effect". The old game handled input between two frames, before the frame's own work, so a view change asked for that way came one frame sooner (in the old fight only one can be: stabEnd, when the super move is started during stab mode).
other.fadeToBlack: The fade to black that ends a round is a screen flash of the interface in the old build, not the camera: it starts 0.82 x the dying clip's length after the fatal blow and takes 0.162 x that length.
other.enemyView: The battle levels also hold a slow orbit around the enemy ("Boss_Camera1"). The old fight never asks for it (it was for a human-played enemy), so it is not here.
other.clock: Some cues carry `clock`: what the old fight does to its own clock at that moment — a game speed, how many real seconds it lasts, a hit pause. The camera does none of it; the game does, and passes its speed to update().
other.unused: In the old data and never played by anything: the stab shots of the campaign levels ("Stab1..3": a lower camera zooming in), and the camera animations Magic_Heal, Magic_Push, Magic_Shield, Hero_ShieldSmash, Hero_Dodge_Left.
